units.zh: 薛廷珪，其先河東人也。
units.en: Xue Tinggui came of a Hedong family.
units.literal: Xue Tinggui — his ancestors were people of Hedong.

units.zh: 父逢，咸通中為秘書監，以才名著於時。
units.en: His father Feng served as Director of the Palace Library under Emperor Yizong and was widely celebrated for his gifts as a writer.
units.literal: His father Feng, during the Xiantong reign period served as Director of the Palace Library, and was renowned in his time for literary talent.

units.zh: 廷珪，中和年在西川登進士第，累曆台省。
units.en: Tinggui earned his jinshi degree in Sichuan during the Zhonghe era and rose through a series of central-government posts.
units.literal: Tinggui, in the Zhonghe years passed the jinshi examination in Xichuan, and successively held posts in the central secretariats.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：大順初，累遷司勳員外郎、知制誥。）〉
units.en: (According to the Old Book of Tang, in early Dashun he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and commissioner for drafting imperial edicts.)〉
units.literal: (Old Book of Tang: At the beginning of the Dashun reign he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and to Drafting Commissioner.)〉

units.zh: 乾寧中，為中書舍人。
units.en: During the Qianning era he served as a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
units.literal: During Qianning, he was a Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 駕在華州，改散騎常侍，尋請致仕，客遊蜀川。
units.en: While the court was at Huazhou he was made Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then soon asked to retire and lived for a time as a guest in Sichuan.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Huazhou, he was reassigned as Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he requested retirement from office and traveled as a guest in Shu.

units.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，征為禮部侍郎。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong relocated to Luoyang, Tinggui was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光化中，復為中書舍人，遷邢部、吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。）〉
units.en: (The Old Book of Tang adds that in the Guanghua era he again became a Secretariat drafting secretary, rose to vice minister of punishments and of personnel, temporarily supervised the civil-service examinations for the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
units.literal: (Old Book of Tang: In Guanghua he again became Secretariat Drafting Secretary, was promoted to Vice Ministers of Punishments and of Personnel, acted as provisional overseer of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

units.zh: 時柳璨屠害朝士，衣冠畢罹其毒，廷珪以居常退讓獲全。
units.en: When Liu Can was butchering court officials, the entire official class fell victim to him; Tinggui alone escaped harm through his habitual modesty and restraint.
units.literal: At that time Liu Can slaughtered court officials; the gentry all suffered his poison, but Tinggui was spared because of his usual modesty and yielding conduct.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：朱全忠兼四鎮，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜。
units.en: (The New Book of Tang records that when Zhu Quanzhong held four military circuits at once, Tinggui came to Bian as the bearer of his commission of office. A host officer received him first and suggested obliquely that he should bow.
units.literal: (New Book of Tang: Zhu Quanzhong held four circuits concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as commissioner bearing the patent of office, and a guest officer who met him first hinted that he should bow.

units.zh: 廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎！」
units.en: Tinggui feigned not to understand and said, "What merit have I that I should accept a bow from Your Lordship!"
units.literal: Tinggui pretended not to understand, saying: "What virtue do I have, that I dare receive the Lord Commander's bow!"

units.zh: 及見，卒不肯加禮。）〉
units.en: When they met face to face, he still refused to offer the courtesy.)〉
units.literal: When they met, he in the end refused to add the courtesy.)〉

units.zh: 入梁為禮部尚書。
units.en: Under the Liang he became Minister of Rites.
units.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 莊宗平定河南，以廷珪年老，除太子少師致仕。
units.en: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Tinggui was granted retirement as Mentor of the Heir Apparent on account of his advanced age.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, because Tinggui was old he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent with junior third rank and retired.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：廷珪與李琪嘗為太祖冊禮使。）〉
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian notes that Tinggui and Li Qi had once served together as ritual commissioners for Taizu's investiture.)〉
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi once served as enfeoffment ritual commissioners for Taizu.)〉

units.zh: 同光三年九月卒。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of Tongguang 3 (925).
units.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang he died.

units.zh: 贈右僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 所著《鳳閣詞書》十卷、《克家志》五卷，並行於世。
units.en: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings, in ten fascicles, and Record of Honoring the Family, in five fascicles, both circulated widely.
units.literal: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings in ten fascicles and Record of Honoring the Family in five fascicles both circulated in the world.

units.zh: 初，廷珪父逢，著《鑿混沌》、《真珠簾》等賦，大為時人所稱。
units.en: Tinggui's father Feng had earlier written celebrated rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain that won wide praise in their day.
units.literal: Earlier, Tinggui's father Feng had composed rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain, which were greatly praised by people of the time.

units.zh: 廷珪既壯，亦著賦數十篇，同為一集，故目曰《克家志》。
units.en: When Tinggui came of age he too wrote several dozen rhapsodies and collected them in one volume, which he titled Record of Honoring the Family.
units.literal: When Tinggui reached maturity, he also composed several dozen rhapsodies, gathered into one collection, hence its title Record of Honoring the Family.

units.zh: 崔沂，
units.en: Cui Yi,
units.literal: Cui Yi,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世係表》：沂，字德潤。）〉
units.en: (The New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers give his style name as Derun.)〉
units.literal: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yi, style name Derun.)〉

units.zh: 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也。
units.en: He was the youngest son of Cui Xuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor in the Dazhong era.
units.literal: He was the youngest son of Grand Councilor Duke of Wei Gongxuan of the Dazhong era.

units.zh: 兄沆，廣明初亦為宰輔。
units.en: His elder brother Hong likewise reached the chief ministership early in the Guangming era.
units.literal: His elder brother Hong, at the beginning of Guangming also became a chief minister.

units.zh: 沂舉進士第，曆監察、補闕。
units.en: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as investigating censor and remonstrance official.
units.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor and Reminder.

units.zh: 昭宗時，累遷至員外郎、知制誥。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose in stages to outer-court director and drafting commissioner.
units.literal: During Zhaozong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director and Drafting Commissioner.

units.zh: 性抗厲守道，而文藻非優，嘗與同舍顏蕘、錢珝俱秉筆，見蕘、珝贍速，草制數十，無妨譚笑，而沂自愧。
units.en: Firm and principled by nature, he was not a gifted stylist. Once, drafting edicts alongside colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, he watched them turn out dozens of documents with ease, chatting and laughing all the while, and was mortified by his own slowness.
units.literal: By nature he was stern and upheld the Way, but his literary polish was not superior; once he drafted together with colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, and seeing Rao and Pei swift and ample, drafting several dozen edicts without hindering banter, Yi felt ashamed of himself.

units.zh: 翌日，謁國相訴曰：「沂疏淺，不足以供詞翰之職。」
units.en: The next day he called on the chief minister and said, "I am too shallow a writer to hold a drafting post."
units.literal: The next day he called on the chief minister and pleaded: "Yi is shallow and insufficient to fulfill the duties of literary drafting."

units.zh: 相輔然之，移為諫議大夫。
units.en: The minister concurred and moved him to the post of Grand Master of Remonstrance.
units.literal: The minister agreed and transferred him to Grand Censor.

units.zh: 入梁，為御史司憲，糾繆繩違，不避豪右。
units.en: Under the Liang he headed the Censorate, correcting abuses and enforcing the law without fear of the powerful.
units.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Director of the Censorate, correcting errors and restraining violations, not avoiding powerful families.

units.zh: 開平中，金吾街使寇彥卿入朝，過天津橋，市民梁現者不時回避，前導伍伯捽之，投石欄以致斃。
units.en: During Kaiping, Jinwu street commissioner Kou Yanqing came to court and crossed Tianjin Bridge. A townsman named Liang Xian failed to clear the way in time; Kou's escort guards seized him and hurled him against a stone railing, killing him.
units.literal: During Kaiping, Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing entered court audience, passed Tianjin Bridge, and a townsman named Liang Xian failed to withdraw in time; the forward escort guards seized him and threw him against a stone railing, causing death.

units.zh: 彥卿自前白於梁祖，梁祖命通事舍人趙可封宣諭，令出私財與死者之家，以贖其罪。
units.en: Yanqing reported the matter himself to the Liang founder, who ordered palace usher Zhao Kefeng to announce that Yanqing should pay compensation from his private funds to the victim's family in lieu of punishment.
units.literal: Yanqing himself went forward to report to the Liang founder; the founder ordered Palace Usher Zhao Kefeng to announce the instruction, directing him to pay private funds to the dead man's family to redeem his offense.

units.zh: 沂奏劾曰：「彥卿位是人臣，無專殺之理。
units.en: Yi submitted an impeachment memorial: "Yanqing is a subject of the throne and has no right to kill on his own authority.
units.literal: Yi memorialized in impeachment: "Yanqing's position is that of a subject; there is no principle of unauthorized killing.

units.zh: 況天津橋御路之要，正對端門，當車駕出入之途，非街使震怒之所。
units.en: Moreover Tianjin Bridge lies on the main imperial thoroughfare, directly before the Gate of Propriety, on the very path the imperial carriage takes; it is no place for a street commissioner to vent his anger.
units.literal: Moreover Tianjin Bridge is a vital point on the imperial roadway, directly facing the Gate of Propriety, on the route of the imperial carriage's coming and going — not a place for a street commissioner to vent rage.

units.zh: 況梁現不時回避，其過止於鞭笞。
units.en: As for Liang Xian's failure to clear the way in time, the offense warranted no more than a beating.
units.literal: Moreover Liang Xian's failure to withdraw in time — his offense goes no further than flogging.

units.zh: 捽首投驅，深乖朝憲，請論之以法。」
units.en: To seize a man and dash him to death so flagrantly violates the statutes; I ask that he be prosecuted according to law."
units.literal: Seizing him by the head and casting him to death deeply violates court statutes; I request that he be judged by law."

units.zh: 梁祖惜彥卿，令沂以過失論，沂引鬥競律，以怙勢力為罪首，下手者減一等。
units.en: The Liang founder was reluctant to punish Yanqing and told Yi to treat the case as negligence. Yi cited the statute on brawling, naming abuse of power as the principal offense and reducing the penalty by one degree for those who carried out the act.
units.literal: The Liang founder valued Yanqing and ordered Yi to judge it as a case of negligence; Yi cited the statute on brawling, making reliance on power the chief offense and reducing one degree for those who carried it out.

units.zh: 又鬥毆條，不鬥故毆傷人者，加傷罪一等。
units.en: He also invoked the article on assault: anyone who, without a prior fight, deliberately beats and injures another has the injury charge increased by one degree.
units.literal: He also cited the article on fighting: one who without fighting deliberately beats and injures a person has the injury offense increased by one degree.

units.zh: 沂表入，責授彥卿遊擊將軍、左衛中郎將。
units.en: When Yi's memorial was received, Yanqing was demoted to general of the patrol and middle general of the Left Guard.
units.literal: When Yi's memorial entered, Yanqing was demoted and appointed General of the Patrol and Middle General of the Left Guard.

units.zh: 沂剛正守法，人士多之。
units.en: Yi's stern integrity in upholding the law won him wide admiration among the official class.
units.literal: Yi was upright and upheld the law; scholars and officials greatly admired him.

units.zh: 遷左司侍郎，改太常卿，轉禮部尚書。
units.en: He was promoted to vice director of the left secretariat, then made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later minister of rites.
units.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 貞明中，帶本官充西京副留守。
units.en: During Zhenming he served as deputy protector-general of the Western Capital while retaining his ministerial title.
units.literal: During Zhenming, while retaining his original office he served as Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.

units.zh: 時張全義留守、天下兵馬副元帥、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、中書令、魏王，名位之重，冠絕中外。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi then held the posts of protector-general, deputy commander-in-chief of all forces, prefect of Henan, controller of the six armies and all guards, acting grand preceptor, grand secretariat director, and Prince of Wei — titles whose weight surpassed every other figure at court or in the provinces.
units.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi was Protector-General, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Prefect of Henan, Controller of the Six Armies and All Guards, Acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Secretariat Director, and Prince of Wei — the weight of his titles and position surpassed all within and without the court.

units.zh: 沂至府，客將白以副留守合行廷禮，沂曰：「張公官位至重，然尚帶府尹之名，不知副留守見尹之儀何如？」
units.en: When Yi arrived at headquarters, a staff officer told him that as deputy protector he was expected to perform court ceremony. Yi replied, "Lord Zhang's rank is immense, yet he still holds the title of prefect — I am not sure what protocol a deputy protector should follow in meeting a prefect?"
units.literal: When Yi arrived at the headquarters, a guest officer reported that as deputy protector he ought to perform court ritual; Yi said: "Lord Zhang's office and rank are extremely weighty, yet he still bears the title of prefect — I do not know what ceremony the deputy protector should use in meeting the prefect."

units.zh: 全義知之，遽引見沂，勞曰：「彼此有禮，俱老矣，勿相勞煩。」
units.en: Quanyi heard of this, summoned Yi at once, and said kindly, "Let us observe courtesy between equals — we are both old men; spare each other the formalities."
units.literal: Quanyi learned of this, hurriedly received Yi in audience, and comforted him: "Between us there is mutual courtesy; we are both old — do not trouble each other with formalities."

units.zh: 莊宗興復唐室，復用為左丞，判吏部尚書銓選司，坐累謫石州司馬。
units.en: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang, Yi was again appointed left vice director and placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau; he was later demoted to defender of Shizhou on accumulated charges.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang house, Yi was again employed as Left Vice Director, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel selection bureau; through accumulated offenses he was demoted to Defender of Shizhou.

units.zh: 明宗即位，召還，復為左丞。
units.en: When Mingzong came to the throne, Yi was recalled and restored as left vice director.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and again made Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 以衰疾告老，授太子少保致仕。
units.en: Citing age and illness, he petitioned to retire and was granted the post of junior mentor of the heir apparent with retirement honors.
units.literal: Because of age and illness he requested retirement and was granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement.

units.zh: 卒於龍門之別墅，時年七十餘。
units.en: He died at his villa in Longmen at over seventy years of age.
units.literal: He died at a villa in Longmen, aged over seventy.

units.zh: 贈太子少傅。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as junior tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 劉岳，字昭輔。
units.en: Liu Yue, whose style was Zhaofu.
units.literal: Liu Yue, style name Zhaofu.

units.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。
units.en: His forebears came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified the northeast the family was moved to Dai; they followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang and became Luoyang natives.
units.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, followed Emperor Xiaowen in the move to Luoyang, and thus became Luoyang people.

units.zh: 八代祖民部尚書渝國公政會，武德時功臣。
units.en: Eight generations back stood Zhenghui, minister of the household and Duke of Yu, a founding merit-holder of the Wude era.
units.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhenghui, Minister of the Household and Duke of Yu of the Yu State, was a meritorious minister of the Wude era.

units.zh: 祖符，蔡州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Fu had been prefect of Cai.
units.literal: His grandfather Fu was Prefect of Cai.

units.zh: 父珪，洪洞縣令。
units.en: His father Gui served as magistrate of Hongtong County.
units.literal: His father Gui was Magistrate of Hongtong County.

units.zh: 符有子八人，皆登進士第。
units.en: Fu had eight sons, every one of whom passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: Fu had eight sons, all of whom passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 珪之母弟瑰、玕，異母弟崇夷、崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨。
units.en: The father Gui's full brothers were Kui and Gan; his half-brothers were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.
units.literal: Gui the father's younger brothers by the same mother were Kui and Gan; younger brothers by a different mother were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.

units.zh: 崇龜，乾寧中廣南節度使；
units.en: Chonggui served as military commissioner of Guangnan during Qianning;
units.literal: Chonggui, during Qianning was Military Commissioner of Guangnan;

units.zh: 崇望，乾寧中宰相；
units.en: Chongwang was chief minister in the same era;
units.literal: Chongwang, during Qianning was chief minister;

units.zh: 崇魯、崇謨、崇夷，並曆朝省。
units.en: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all held posts in the central ministries.
units.literal: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all successively served in the central ministries.

units.zh: 嶽少孤，亦進士擢第，曆戶部巡官、鄭縣簿、直史館，轉左拾遺、侍御史。
units.en: Orphaned young, Yue also earned his jinshi degree and served in succession as a touring official in the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian in the History Office, then as left remonstrance official and attending censor.
units.literal: Yue was orphaned young; he also passed the jinshi examination, successively served as touring official of the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian of the History Office, and was transferred to Left Reminder and Attending Censor.

units.zh: 梁貞明初，召入翰林為學士。
units.en: Early in Liang Zhenming he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
units.literal: At the beginning of Liang Zhenming he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

units.zh: 嶽為文敏速，尤善談諧，在職累遷戶部侍郎，在翰林十二年。
units.en: Yue wrote with quick facility and had a gift for witty conversation. He rose to vice minister of revenue and spent twelve years in the Hanlin.
units.literal: Yue wrote with quick facility and was especially skilled at witty conversation; in office he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served in the Hanlin for twelve years.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，隨例貶均州司馬，尋丁母憂，許自貶所奔喪，服闋，授太子詹事。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yue was demoted under the usual purge to defender of Junzhou. He soon entered mourning for his mother and was allowed to leave his post of exile for the funeral; when the mourning ended he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, following precedent he was demoted to Defender of Junzhou; soon he entered mourning for his mother, was permitted to rush home for the funeral from his place of demotion, and after the mourning period was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 明宗即位，曆兵部吏部侍郎、秘書監、太常卿。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served in succession as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, director of the Palace Library, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Palace Library, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 卒年五十六。
units.en: He died at fifty-six.
units.literal: He died at age fifty-six.

units.zh: 贈吏部尚書。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as minister of personnel.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 岳文學之外，通於典禮。
units.en: Apart from his literary gifts, Yue was deeply versed in ritual protocol.
units.literal: Beyond his literary learning, Yue was versed in ritual regulations.

units.zh: 天成中，奉詔撰《新書儀》一部，文約而理當，今行於世。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was ordered to compile the New Book of Ritual — concise in wording and sound in principle — which remains in use today.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled one work, New Book of Ritual, concise in text and correct in principle, which circulates in the world today.

units.zh: 子溫叟，仕至御史中丞。
units.en: His son Wensou rose to censor-in-chief.
units.literal: His son Wensou served up to Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：劉溫叟方正守道，以名教為己任。
units.en: (The Statesmen's Garden of Talk records that Liu Wensou was upright and principled, holding himself to the standards of proper conduct.
units.literal: (Statesmen's Garden of Talk says: Liu Wensou was upright and upheld the Way, taking name and teaching as his personal charge.

units.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞，其母甚賢。
units.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for filial devotion to his mother, who was a woman of exceptional virtue.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he was known for filial service to his mother; his mother was very worthy.

units.zh: 初為翰林學士，私庭拜母，母即命二婢箱擎公服、金帶，置於階下，謂溫叟曰：「此汝父長興中入翰林時所賜也。
units.en: When he first became a Hanlin academician, he bowed to his mother in their private courtyard. She at once had two maidservants bring out chests holding official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps, saying, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.
units.literal: When he first became Hanlin academician, in the private courtyard he bowed to his mother; his mother immediately ordered two maidservants to carry in chests the official robes and gold belt, and set them on the steps below, saying to Wensou: "These were bestowed when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.

units.zh: 自先君子薨背以來，嘗懼家門替墜，今汝能自致青雲，繼父之職，可服之無愧矣！」
units.en: Since your father's death I have feared our house would fall into decline. Now you have risen on your own merits to succeed to his post — wear them without shame!"
units.literal: Since your late father's passing I have feared the family's decline; now you can reach the blue clouds on your own, succeeding to your father's office — you may wear them without shame!"

units.zh: 因欷歔掩泣。
units.en: With that she sighed and wept, covering her face.
units.literal: Thereupon she sighed and sobbed, covering her face with tears.

units.zh: 溫叟伏地號慟，退就別寢，素衣蔬食，追慕數日，然後服之，士大夫以為得禮。）〉
units.en: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed aloud, then withdrew to another room, dressed in plain clothes and ate simple fare, and mourned his father for several days before putting on the robes. Men of cultivation held this to be proper ritual.)〉
units.literal: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed loudly; he withdrew to a separate chamber, wore plain clothes and ate simple food, mourned in remembrance for several days, and only then donned the robes — the gentry considered this proper ritual.)〉

units.zh: 封舜卿，
units.en: Feng Shunqing,
units.literal: Feng Shunqing,

units.literal: (Note: the original text has lacunae.

units.zh: 據《新唐書·宰相世係表》，封氏世居渤海蓚縣。
units.en: According to the New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers, the Feng clan had long resided in Tiao County in Bohai.
units.literal: According to the New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers, the Feng clan for generations dwelt in Raoyang County, Bohai.

units.zh: 舜卿，字讚聖，父敖，字碩夫，戶部尚書、渤海縣男。
units.en: Shunqing's style was Zansheng. His father Ao, style Shuofu, had been minister of revenue and Baron of Bohai County.
units.literal: Shunqing, style name Zansheng; his father Ao, style name Shuofu, was Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai County.

units.zh: 《唐書》有傳。）〉
units.en: The Book of Tang contains his biography.)〉
units.literal: The Book of Tang has his biography.)〉

units.zh: 仕梁，為禮部侍郎，知貢舉。
units.en: Under the Liang he served as vice minister of rites and supervised the civil-service examinations.
units.literal: Serving the Liang, he was Vice Minister of Rites and oversaw the examinations.

units.zh: 開平三年，奉使幽州，以門生鄭致雍從行，復命之日，又與致雍同受命入翰林為學士。
units.en: In Kaiping 3 (909) he was sent on a mission to Youzhou with his protégé Zheng Zhiyong as companion. On the day he reported back, both men were appointed Hanlin academicians.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, on a mission to Youzhou, he took his student Zheng Zhiyong to accompany him; on the day of reporting back, both he and Zhiyong received orders to enter the Hanlin as academicians.

units.zh: 致雍有俊才，舜卿雖有文辭，才思拙澀，及試五題，不勝困弊，因托致雍秉筆，當時譏者以為座主辱門生。
units.en: Zhiyong was brilliantly gifted. Shunqing had literary polish but slow, labored invention; when tested on five topics he was overwhelmed and asked Zhiyong to draft for him — contemporaries mocked it as a patron disgracing his protégé.
units.literal: Zhiyong had brilliant talent; although Shunqing had literary polish, his creative thought was clumsy and slow, and when tested on five topics he could not bear the strain, so he entrusted Zhiyong to wield the brush — contemporaries mocked this as the examination patron shaming his student.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (The text is defective from this point.)〉
units.literal: (Note: below there are lacunae.)〉

units.zh: 莊宗同光已來，累曆清顯。
units.en: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang era onward he held a series of high, prestigious posts.
units.literal: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang onward, he successively held pure and eminent offices.

units.zh: 封氏自太和以來，世居兩製，以文筆稱於時。
units.en: Since the Taihe era the Feng family had for generations held the two chief drafting posts and were famed for their literary skill.
units.literal: The Feng clan from the Taihe era onward for generations held the two drafting posts, renowned in their time for literary brushwork.

units.zh: 舜卿從子渭，
units.en: Shunqing's nephew Wei,
units.literal: Shunqing's nephew Wei,

units.zh: 〈（《世係表》：渭，字希叟。）〉
units.en: (The genealogical tables give his style as Xisou.)〉
units.literal: (Genealogical Tables: Wei, style name Xisou.)〉

units.zh: 昭宗遷洛時，為翰林學士，舜卿為中書舍人，叔侄對掌內外製。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wei was a Hanlin academician while Shunqing was a Secretariat drafting secretary — uncle and nephew together controlled inner and outer edict drafting.
units.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was Hanlin academician while Shunqing was Secretariat Drafting Secretary — uncle and nephew jointly held inner and outer drafting.

units.zh: 從子翹，於梁貞明中亦為翰林學士。
units.en: His nephew Qiao likewise became a Hanlin academician during Liang Zhenming.
units.literal: His nephew Qiao, during Liang Zhenming also became Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 天成中，為給事中，因轉對上言，以星辰合度，風雨應時，請御前香一合，帝親爇一炷，餘令於塔廟中焚之，貴表精至。
units.en: During Tiancheng he served as supervising censor. In a rotating audience he reported that the heavens and seasons were in harmony and asked for incense before the throne. The emperor burned one stick himself and had the rest offered at pagodas and temples — a gesture of rare devotion.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was Supervising Censor; in a rotating audience memorial he stated that the stars and planets were in accord and wind and rain came in season, requesting one measure of incense before the throne — the emperor personally burned one stick, and ordered the remainder burned at pagodas and temples, showing precious sincerity.

units.zh: 議者以翹時推名族，出朝苑，登瑣闈，甚有岩廊之望，而忽有此請，乃近諸妖佞耳，物望由是減之。
units.en: Critics said Qiao, a man of eminent lineage who had risen from the Hanlin to high office with every prospect of reaching the chief councils, had suddenly made a request fit for sorcerers and sycophants — and his reputation never recovered.
units.literal: Commentators held that Qiao was then esteemed as a great-clan figure who had left the court garden and ascended the privy gate, with great prospects for the state council — yet suddenly making such a request was close to the ways of sorcerers and flatterers, and public esteem for him diminished accordingly.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下殘闕。）〉
units.en: (The text is defective from this point.)〉
units.literal: (Note: below the text is defective.)〉

units.zh: 竇夢徵，同州人。
units.en: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.
units.literal: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 少苦心為文，登進士第，曆校書郎，自拾遺召入翰林，充學士。
units.en: He devoted himself to letters from youth, passed the jinshi examination, served as proofreader, and was summoned from the remonstrance post into the Hanlin as an academician.
units.literal: In youth he labored at writing, passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader, and from Reminder was summoned into the Hanlin to serve as academician.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，加兩浙錢鏐元帥之命。
units.en: During Liang Zhenming the court issued an edict making Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits grand marshal.
units.literal: During Liang Zhenming, the commission of Grand Marshal was conferred on Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits.

units.zh: 夢徵以鏐無功於中原，兵柄不宜虛授，其言切直。
units.en: Mengzheng argued that Liu had done nothing for the central realm and that military command should not be handed out lightly. His memorial was blunt and uncompromising.
units.literal: Mengzheng held that Liu had rendered no service to the central plains and that military authority ought not be granted in vain; his words were sharp and direct.

units.zh: 梁末帝以觸時忌，左授外任。
units.en: The Last Liang Emperor, offended by his candor, demoted him to a provincial post.
units.literal: The Last Liang Emperor, because he had touched a taboo of the times, demoted him to an outside post.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇以錢公無功於本朝，僻在一方，坐邀恩澤，不稱是命，乃抱麻哭於朝。
units.en: (Jade Hall Idle Talk records that Dou argued Lord Qian had done nothing for the dynasty yet sat in a remote corner receiving favors unearned by merit. Deeming the commission unfitting, he embraced the mourning hemp and wept in open court.
units.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou held that Lord Qian had rendered no service to the dynasty, dwelt remote in one region, and yet sat receiving grace — the commission did not fit; he therefore embraced the hemp mourning garb and wept at court.

units.zh: 翌日，竇謫掾於東州。）〉
units.en: The next day Dou was banished to serve as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉
units.literal: The next day Dou was banished as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉

units.zh: 有頃，復召為學士。
units.en: Before long he was recalled as a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: Before long he was again summoned as academician.

units.zh: 及莊宗入汴，夢徵以例貶沂州，居嘗感梁末帝舊恩，因為《祭故君文》云：「嗚呼！
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under the usual purge to Yizhou. Grateful still for the Last Liang Emperor's past kindness, he wrote A Eulogy for the Former Lord, which begins: "Alas!
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under precedent to Yizhou; dwelling there he often felt the old grace of the Last Liang Emperor, and therefore composed A Eulogy for the Former Lord, saying: "Alas!

units.zh: 四海九州，天回眷命，一女二夫，人之不幸。
units.en: Across the realm Heaven has shifted its mandate — like one woman with two husbands, a thing no loyal subject can bear without grief.
units.literal: Within the four seas and nine provinces, Heaven turns its favor — one woman, two husbands: man's misfortune.

units.zh: 當革故以鼎新，若金銷而火盛，必然之理，夫何足競」云。
units.en: When the old must give way to the new, as metal melts in a raging fire — such is necessity; what is there to struggle against?" and so forth.
units.literal: When the old must be changed for the new, as metal melts and fire blazes — the necessary principle — what is there to contend over," and so on.

units.zh: 秉筆者皆許之，尋量移宿州。
units.en: Fellow writers praised the piece, and he was soon transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.
units.literal: The drafters all praised it; soon he was transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.

units.zh: 天成初，遷中書舍人，復入為翰林學士、工部侍郎。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he was made a Secretariat drafting secretary, then again entered the Hanlin and rose to vice minister of works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary, again entered service as Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。
units.en: He died and was posthumously ennobled as minister of rites.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇失意被謫，嘗鬱鬱不樂，曾夢有人謂曰：「君無自苦，不久當復故職。
units.en: (Jade Hall Idle Talk adds that Dou, disheartened in exile, grew despondent. In a dream someone told him, "Do not torment yourself — you will soon return to your former post.
units.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou, disheartened in banishment, was often depressed; once he dreamed someone said: "Do not torment yourself — before long you will return to your former office.

units.zh: 然將來慎勿為丞相，苟有是命，當萬計避之。」
units.en: But hereafter beware of becoming chief minister. If such an appointment should come, avoid it by every means you can."
units.literal: Yet in the future be careful never to become chief minister; if such a command should come, you must by every means avoid it."

units.zh: 其後竇復居禁職。
units.en: He later returned to a palace post.
units.literal: Afterward Dou again held a forbidden-office post.

units.zh: 有頃，遷工部侍郎。
units.en: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of works.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 竇忽憶夢中所言，深惡其事。
units.en: Dou suddenly remembered the dream and dreaded what it foretold.
units.literal: Dou suddenly recalled what was said in the dream and deeply dreaded that matter.

units.zh: 然已受命，不能遜避，未幾果卒。）〉
units.en: Yet he had already accepted the appointment and could not refuse. Before long he died, just as the dream had warned.)〉
units.literal: Yet he had already received the command and could not decline; before long he indeed died.)〉

units.zh: 夢徵隨計之秋，文稱甚高，尤長於箋啟，編為十卷，目曰《東堂集》，行於世。
units.en: At the time of his civil-service examination his writing won high praise. He excelled especially at letters and memorials, which were collected in ten fascicles as Eastern Hall Collection and circulated widely.
units.literal: In the autumn of Mengzheng's examination journey his writing was greatly acclaimed; he was especially skilled at letters and memorials, compiled in ten fascicles under the title Eastern Hall Collection, circulating in the world.

units.zh: 李保殷，河南洛陽人也。
units.en: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
units.literal: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

units.zh: 昭宗朝，自處士除太子正字，改錢塘縣尉。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose from recluse scholar to proofreader of the heir apparent, then became magistrate of Qiantang County.
units.literal: During Zhaozong's reign, from Recluse Scholar he was appointed Proofreader of the Heir Apparent, then changed to Magistrate of Qiantang County.

units.zh: 浙東帥董昌辟為推官，調補河府兵曹參軍，曆長水令、《毛詩》博士，累官至太常少卿、端王傅。
units.en: Dong Chang, military commissioner of eastern Zhe, recruited him as investigating officer. He was transferred to a staff post in the He prefecture, served as magistrate of Changshui and doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and tutor to the Prince of Duan.
units.literal: The Zhedong military commissioner Dong Chang recruited him as investigating officer; he was transferred to fill a post as military staff officer of the He prefecture, successively served as Magistrate of Changshui and Doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with junior third rank and Tutor of the Prince of Duan.

units.zh: 入為大理卿，撰《刑律總要》十二卷；
units.en: He entered the capital as director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;
units.literal: He entered service as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;

units.zh: 與兵部侍郎郗殷象論刑法事。
units.en: and discussed penal law with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang.
units.literal: and with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang discussed matters of penal law.

units.zh: 左降房州司馬。
units.en: He was demoted to defender of Fangzhou.
units.literal: He was demoted to Defender of Fangzhou.

units.zh: 同光初，授殿中監，以其素有明法律之譽，拜大理卿；
units.en: Early in Tongguang he was made director of the palace domestic service and, on his long-standing reputation for legal expertise, was appointed director of judicial review;
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service; because he had long enjoyed a reputation for mastery of law, he was appointed Director of Judicial Review;

units.zh: 未滿秩，屬為人所製。
units.en: but before his term ended he was framed by enemies.
units.literal: before his term was complete, he happened to be framed by others.

units.zh: 保殷曰：「人之多辟，無自立辟。」
units.en: Baoyin said, "When the world is full of crime, do not make yourself a criminal."
units.literal: Baoyin said: "When many people commit offenses, do not create offenses for yourself."

units.zh: 乃謝病以歸，卒於洛陽。
units.en: He pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang, where he died.
units.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home, dying in Luoyang.

units.zh: 歸藹，字文彥，吳郡人也。
units.en: Gui Ai, whose style was Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.
units.literal: Gui Ai, style name Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 曾祖登，祖融，父仁澤，位皆至列曹尚書、觀察使。
units.en: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to ranking secretariat posts and military commissioner.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to the posts of ranking secretary in the boards and military commissioner.

units.zh: 藹登進士第，及升朝，遍曆三署。
units.en: Ai passed the jinshi examination and, once he entered court service, served in turn in all three secretariat offices.
units.literal: Ai passed the jinshi examination; when he entered court service he served in turn in all three secretariat offices.
