units.en: (Below there is suspected missing text.
units.literal: (Note: below there is suspected missing text.

units.zh: 據《舊唐書·昭宗紀》：天祐元年七月，宴於文思殿。
units.en: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang, in the seventh month of Tianyou 1 (904) a banquet was held in Wensi Hall.
units.literal: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianyou, a banquet was held in the Wensi Hall.

units.zh: 朱全忠入，百官或坐於廊下，全忠怒，笞通引官何凝。
units.en: When Zhu Quanzhong entered, some officials were seated in the corridor below. Quanzhong was enraged and had the usher He Ning flogged.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong entered; some of the hundred officials were seated in the corridor below, and Quanzhong was angered and had the usher He Ning flogged.

units.zh: 丙寅，製金紫光祿大夫、行御史中丞、上柱國韓儀責授棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹責授登州司戶，坐百官傲全忠也。）
units.en: On bingyin an edict demoted Han Yi, grand master of the golden glow and purple ornament, acting censor, and supreme pillar of state, to defender of Dizhou, and remonstrating censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou, for the offense of officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)
units.literal: On bingyin, an edict demoted Grand Master of the Golden Glow and Purple Ornament, Acting Censor, and Supreme Pillar of State Han Yi to defender of Dizhou, and Remonstrating Censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou—for the offense of the hundred officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)

units.zh: 同光初，為尚書右丞，遷刑、戶二部侍郎，以太子賓客致仕，卒年七十六。
units.en: Early in Tongguang he served as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as honorary attendant to the crown prince, and died at seventy-six.
units.literal: Early in Tongguang he served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as Honorary Attendant to the Crown Prince, and died at seventy-six.

units.zh: 孔邈，文宣王四十一代孫。
units.en: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of Confucius.
units.literal: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of the Cultured Propagator King.

units.zh: 身長七尺餘，神氣溫厚。
units.en: He stood over seven chi tall, with a warm and dignified bearing.
units.literal: His body was over seven chi in height; his spirit and bearing were warm and substantial.

units.zh: 登進士第，曆校書郎、萬年尉，充集賢校理，為諫議大夫，以年老致仕。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as proofreader, defender of Wannian district, and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies before becoming grand censor and retiring on account of age.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader and Wannian district defender, acted as collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, became Grand Censor, and retired on account of age.

units.zh: 〈（案：《孔邈傳》，原本殘闕。
units.en: (The received Biography of Kong Miao is defective.
units.literal: (Note: the Biography of Kong Miao in the original is defective.

units.zh: 考《冊府元龜》云：乾寧五年，登進士第，除校書郎。
units.en: The Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm records that in Qianning 5 (898) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.
units.literal: Examining the Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm, it states: In the fifth year of Qianning he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.

units.zh: 崔遠在中書，奏為萬年尉，充集賢校理，以親舅獨孤損方在廊廟，避嫌不赴職。）〉
units.en: Cui Yuan, then in the Secretariat, recommended him as defender of Wannian and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but Miao declined the posts because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was serving in the chief councils and he wished to avoid suspicion.)〉
units.literal: Cui Yuan was in the Secretariat and memorialized appointing him Wannian defender and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was then in the state council, he avoided suspicion and did not take up the post.)〉

units.zh: 張文寶，昭宗朝諫議大夫顗之子也。
units.en: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi, who had served under Emperor Zhaozong.
units.literal: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi of Zhaozong's reign.

units.zh: 文寶初，依河中朱友謙為從事。
units.en: Early in his career Wenbao served on the staff of Zhu Youqian in Hezhong.
units.literal: Early in Wenbao's career he relied on Zhu Youqian of Hezhong as staff member.

units.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以文寶知制誥，曆中書舍人、刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍、知貢舉，遷吏部侍郎。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made drafting commissioner and rose through the posts of Secretariat drafting secretary, vice minister of punishments, left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and examination supervisor before becoming vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made Drafting Commissioner, successively served as Secretariat Drafting Secretary, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and overseer of examinations, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 文寶性雅淡稽古。
units.en: Wenbao was refined, reserved, and devoted to classical learning.
units.literal: Wenbao's nature was refined, restrained, and devoted to antiquity.

units.zh: 長興初，奉使浙中，泛海船壞，水工以小舟救，文寶與副使吏部郎中張絢信風至淮南界，偽吳楊溥禮待甚至，兼厚遺錢幣、食物。
units.en: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his ship was wrecked at sea and sailors rescued him and his party in small boats. Wenbao and his deputy, Personnel Bureau director Zhang Xuan, drifted on the wind to the Huainan border, where Yang Pu of Wu received them with exceptional courtesy and lavished money and provisions on them.
units.literal: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his seagoing vessel was wrecked; sailors rescued them in small boats. Wenbao and the vice-envoy, Personnel Bureau Director Zhang Xuan, trusted the wind and reached the Huainan border; the false Wu ruler Yang Pu received them with extreme courtesy and also gave generous gifts of money and food.

units.zh: 文寶受其食物，反其錢幣，吳人善之，送文寶等復至杭州宣國命，還青州，卒。
units.en: Wenbao accepted the food but returned the money, which won the Wu people's admiration. They escorted him back to Hangzhou to deliver the imperial commission, then he returned to Qingzhou and died.
units.literal: Wenbao accepted their food but returned their money; the Wu people approved, sent Wenbao and the others back to Hangzhou to announce the imperial command, returned to Qingzhou, and died.

units.zh: 子吉，嗣位邑宰。
units.en: His son Ji succeeded to his father's district magistracy.
units.literal: His son Ji succeeded to the district magistracy.

units.zh: 陳乂，薊門人也。
units.en: Chen Yi was a native of Jimen.
units.literal: Chen Yi was a man of Jimen.

units.zh: 少好學，善屬文。
units.en: From youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 因避亂，客於浮陽，轉徙於大梁。
units.en: To escape the turmoil he lived as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.
units.literal: To escape the turmoil he stayed as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.

units.zh: 梁將張漢傑延於私邸，表授太子舍人。
units.en: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as attendant of the heir apparent.
units.literal: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 莊宗平梁，郭崇韜遙領常山，召居賓榻。
units.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.

units.zh: 崇韜從魏王繼岌伐蜀，署為招討判官。
units.en: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.
units.literal: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.

units.zh: 崇韜死，明宗即位，隨任圜歸闕，圜薦之於朝，除膳部員外郎、知制誥，累遷中書舍人。
units.en: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court. Yuan recommended him, and he was appointed vice director of the Board of Provisions and drafting commissioner, then rose to Secretariat drafting secretary.
units.literal: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court; Yuan recommended him to the court, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and Drafting Commissioner, then successively promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 乂性陰僻，寡與人合，不為當路所與。
units.en: Yi was secretive and withdrawn, seldom got along with others, and was not favored by those in power.
units.literal: Yi's nature was dark and withdrawn; he seldom got along with others and was not favored by those in power.

units.zh: 尋移左散騎常侍，由是忿以成疾，逾月而卒。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Resentment turned to illness, and after more than a month he died.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; thereby resentment became illness, and after more than a month he died.

units.zh: 乂微有才術，嘗自恃其能。
units.en: Yi had modest talent and once relied heavily on his own ability.
units.literal: Yi had modest talent and skill and once relied on his own ability.

units.zh: 為判官日，人有造者，垂帷深處，罕見其面。
units.en: While serving as an assessor, when visitors came he hung curtains deep within and rarely showed his face.
units.literal: When he was an assessor, if someone came to visit him he would hang curtains deep within and rarely show his face.

units.zh: 及居西掖，而姿態愈倨，位竟不至公卿，蓋器度促狹者也。
units.en: Once he held office in the western secretariat his bearing grew all the more haughty. In the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow.
units.literal: When he held office in the western secretariat his bearing became all the more haughty; in the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow and cramped.

units.zh: 然乂性孤執，尤廉於財。
units.en: Yet Yi was solitary and stubborn and especially scrupulous about money.
units.literal: Yet Yi's nature was solitary and stubborn, and he was especially scrupulous about money.

units.zh: 長興中，嘗自舍人銜命冊晉國公主石氏於太原，晉高祖善待之，但訝其高岸。
units.en: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of Jin at Taiyuan. The Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.
units.literal: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of the Jin state at Taiyuan; the Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.

units.zh: 人或有獻可於乂，宜陳一謳頌以稱晉高祖之美，可邀其厚賄耳。
units.en: Some advised Yi to present a eulogy praising the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.
units.literal: Some advised Yi that he should present a eulogy praising the beauty of the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.

units.zh: 乂曰：「人生貧富，咸有定分，未有持天子命違禮以求利，既損國綱，且虧士行，乂今生所不為也。」
units.en: Yi said, "Whether life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment. No one who bears Heaven's Son's command should violate ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and shames a scholar's conduct. That is something I will never do in this life."
units.literal: Yi said: "Whether one's life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment; there has never been one who held Heaven's Son's command yet violated ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and moreover shames the scholar's conduct; this is something Yi will never do in this life."

units.zh: 聞者嘉之。
units.en: Those who heard praised him.
units.literal: Those who heard praised him.

units.zh: 晉高祖即位，贈禮部尚書。
units.en: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yi was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
units.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 劉讚，魏州人也。
units.en: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 幼有文性。
units.en: He showed literary promise from childhood.
units.literal: In youth he had literary aptitude.

units.zh: 父比，為令錄，誨以詩書，夏月令服青襦單衫。
units.en: His father Bi was a county recorder who taught him the classics and, in summer, made him wear only a plain blue jacket and single-layer shirt.
units.literal: His father Bi served as county recorder; he instructed him with poetry and books, and in summer months ordered him to wear a blue jacket and single-layer shirt.

units.zh: 比每肉食，別置蔬食以飯讚，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也。
units.en: Whenever Bi ate meat he set vegetables before Zan and said, "Meat is an official's perquisite.
units.literal: Whenever Bi ate meat, he set aside vegetable food to feed Zan, saying to him: "Meat is the ruler's salary.

units.zh: 爾欲食肉，當苦心文藝，自可致之，吾祿不可分也。」
units.en: If you want meat, earn it through your own literary merit. I cannot share my salary with you."
units.literal: If you wish to eat meat, you must labor at literary arts — you can obtain it yourself; my salary cannot be shared."

units.zh: 由是讚及冠有文辭，年三十餘登進士第。
units.en: Zan grew into a polished writer and passed the jinshi examination in his thirties.
units.literal: From this Zan by the capping age had literary compositions; in his thirties he passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 魏州節度使羅紹威署巡官，罷歸京師，依開封尹劉鄩。
units.en: Luo Shaowei, military commissioner of Weizhou, appointed him touring officer. When that post ended he went to the capital and attached himself to Kaifeng prefect Liu Yan.
units.literal: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer; when dismissed he returned to the capital and relied on Kaifeng Prefect Liu Yan.

units.zh: 久之，租庸使趙岩表為巡官，累遷至戶部員外郎，職如故。
units.en: Eventually Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan recommended him as touring officer, and he rose to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue while keeping the same duties.
units.literal: After a long time, Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan memorialized him as touring officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director of the Ministry of Revenue, his duties as before.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，租庸副使孔謙以讚里人，表為鹽鐵判官。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, a fellow townsman, recommended Zan as salt and iron commissioner.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, as Zan's fellow townsman, memorialized him as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

units.zh: 天成中，曆知制誥、中書舍人。
units.en: During Tiancheng he served in succession as drafting commissioner and Secretariat drafting secretary.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he successively served as Drafting Commissioner and Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 與學士竇夢徵同年登第，鄰居友善，夢徵卒，讚與同年楊凝式緦麻為位而哭，其家無嫡長，與視喪事，恤其孀稚，人士稱之。
units.en: He had passed the jinshi in the same year as Hanlin academician Dou Mengzheng, and they were friendly neighbors. When Mengzheng died, Zan and his year-mate Yang Ningshi donned hemp mourning and wept at the bier. The family had no eldest son, so Zan helped manage the funeral and cared for the widow and children — conduct widely praised.
units.literal: With academician Dou Mengzheng he had passed the examination in the same year and were friendly neighbors; when Mengzheng died, Zan with his year-mate Yang Ningshi wore hemp mourning and set up a mourning place to weep; the family had no eldest legitimate son — he assisted in overseeing the funeral, comforted the widow and young, and men of cultivation praised him.

units.zh: 改御史中丞、刑部侍郎。
units.en: He was made censor-in-chief and vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 讚性雍和，與物無忤，居官畏慎，人若以私幹之，雖權豪不能移其操。
units.en: Zan was gentle and easy in manner, careful in office, and immovable in principle — even the powerful could not sway him with private appeals.
units.literal: Zan's nature was mild and harmonious; he did not clash with others; in office he was cautious and fearful of error — if people tried to approach him with private requests, even powerful families could not shift his conduct.

units.zh: 未幾，改秘書監，兼秦王傅。
units.en: Before long he was made director of the Palace Library and tutor to the Prince of Qin.
units.literal: Before long he was changed to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Tutor of the Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：秦王為元帥，秦王府判官、太子詹事王居敏與讚鄉曲之舊，以秦王盛年自恣，須朝中選端士納誨，冀其稟畏，乃奏薦讚焉。）〉
units.en: (The Prime Tortoise records that when the Prince of Qin was grand marshal, Wang Jumin, judge of the Qin princely mansion and grand mentor of the heir apparent, an old fellow townsman of Zan, recommended him because the young prince was self-indulgent and needed upright court scholars to admonish him.)〉
units.literal: (Prime Tortoise: The Prince of Qin was Grand Marshal; Qin Prince's Mansion judge and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wang Jumin was an old fellow townsman of Zan; because the Prince of Qin in his prime was self-indulgent, upright scholars from court needed to be selected to offer admonition, hoping he would receive and fear them — therefore he memorialized recommending Zan.)〉

units.zh: 讚節概貞素，忽聞其命，掩泣固辭，竟不能止。
units.en: A man of plain integrity, Zan wept and firmly declined when he heard of the appointment, but could not refuse it.
units.literal: Zan was upright and plain in integrity; suddenly hearing this appointment, he covered his face weeping and firmly declined, but in the end could not be stopped.

units.zh: 〈（案《通鑒》：瓚自以左遷，泣訴，不得免。
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Zan regarded the appointment as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.
units.literal: (Examining the Comprehensive Mirror: Zan regarded it as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.

units.zh: 胡三省注云：唐制，六部侍郎除吏部之外，餘皆從四品下；
units.en: Hu Sanxing notes that under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were junior fourth rank;
units.literal: Hu Sanxing's note states: Under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were all junior fourth rank;

units.zh: 王傅從三品。
units.en: while princely tutors were junior third rank.
units.literal: princely tutors were junior third rank.

units.zh: 然六部侍郎為向用，王傅為左遷，以職事有閑劇之不同也。
units.en: Yet a vice ministry post was a stepping stone to higher office, while a princely tutorship was effectively a demotion, because the duties differed in prestige and influence.
units.literal: Yet vice ministers of the six ministries were posts for advancement, while princely tutors were a demotion — because duties differed in leisure and urgency.

units.zh: 當是時，從榮地居儲副，則秦王傅不可以閑官。
units.en: At that time Congrong held the position of heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor was no sinecure.
units.literal: At that time Congrong's position was as heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor could not be an idle office.

units.zh: 言蓋以從榮輕佻峻急，恐豫其禍，故求脫耳。）〉
units.en: The comment suggests Zan feared Congrong's rash and violent character and sought to escape before disaster struck.)〉
units.literal: The words likely meant that because Congrong was frivolous, sharp, and harsh, he feared sharing in his calamity and therefore sought to escape.)〉

units.zh: 時秦王參佐，皆新進小生，動多輕脫，每稱頌秦王功德，阿意順旨，隻奉談笑，惟讚從容諷議，必獻嘉言。
units.en: The prince's staff were young upstarts, frivolous and eager to flatter. They praised his virtues and joined his revels — only Zan spoke with measured admonition and offered sound counsel.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Qin's staff were all newly risen young men, often frivolous; they constantly praised the prince's merit and virtue, flattered his intent, and attended only to banter — only Zan with composure offered indirect admonition and always presented good counsel.

units.zh: 秦王常接見賓僚及遊客，於酒筵之中，悉令秉筆賦詩。
units.en: The prince often entertained guests and wandering scholars at banquets and required everyone present to compose poetry on the spot.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin often received guests, staff, and traveling scholars; amid wine banquets he ordered all to take brush and compose poetry.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：時從榮溺於篇章，凡門客及通謁遊士，必坐於客次，自出題目，令賦一章，然後接見。）〉
units.en: (The Prime Tortoise adds that Congrong was obsessed with verse. Every retainer and visiting scholar had to wait in the antechamber, compose a poem on a topic the prince set, and only then be received.)〉
units.literal: (Prime Tortoise: At the time Congrong was addicted to literary compositions; all retainers and visiting scholars seeking audience had to sit in the guest wing — he himself set the topic and ordered one rhapsody composed, and only then received them in audience.)〉

units.zh: 讚為師傅，亦與諸客混，然容狀不悅。
units.en: As tutor, Zan was lumped in with the other guests, and his displeasure showed on his face.
units.literal: Zan as tutor was also lumped with the other guests, yet his expression was displeased.

units.zh: 秦王知其意，自是戒典客，讚至勿通，令每月一度至衙。
units.en: The prince understood his feelings and ordered the gatekeeper never to admit him except for one monthly visit to the princely headquarters.
units.literal: The prince knew his mind; from then on he warned the reception officer that when Zan came he was not to be admitted, ordering him to come to the yamen only once a month.

units.zh: 〈（《言行龜鑒》載：劉讚諫秦王曰：「殿下宜以孝敬為職，浮華非所尚也。」
units.en: (The Mirror of Words and Conduct records that Zan admonished the prince: "Your Highness should devote yourself to filial piety and duty. Frivolity is not becoming."
units.literal: (Mirror of Words and Conduct records: Liu Zan admonished the Prince of Qin: "Your Highness ought to take filial piety and respect as your duty; frivolity is not what should be esteemed."

units.zh: 秦王不悅，戒閽者後弗引進。）〉
units.en: The prince took offense and ordered the gatekeepers never to admit him again.)〉
units.literal: The prince was displeased and warned the gatekeepers thereafter not to admit him.)〉

units.zh: 讚既官係王府，不敢朝參，不通慶吊，但閉關喑嗚而已，及秦王得罪，或言讚止於朝降，而讚已服麻衣備驢乘在門矣。
units.en: Bound to the princely household, Zan stopped attending court or paying social calls and lived in seclusion. When the prince fell, some expected Zan merely to accept demotion — but he had already donned hemp mourning and had a donkey waiting at his gate.
units.literal: Zan, since his office was tied to the princely mansion, dared not attend court audience, sent no congratulations or condolences, but only shut his door in silent grief; when the prince was condemned, some said Zan would merely submit to court demotion — yet Zan had already donned hemp mourning and prepared donkey and carriage at his gate.

units.zh: 聞其言曰：「豈有國君之嗣，一旦舉室塗地，而賓佐朝降，得免死，幸也。」
units.en: Hearing this he said, "When an imperial prince's entire household is destroyed overnight, how can his staff merely accept demotion and call themselves fortunate to escape death?"
units.literal: Hearing this he said: "How can there be an heir of the ruler's house whose whole household is suddenly wiped out, while his staff merely submit to court demotion — to escape death is fortune."

units.zh: 俄而台史示敕，長流嵐州，即時赴貶所。
units.en: Soon the censorate edict arrived banishing him to Lanzhou, and he set out at once.
units.literal: Soon the censorate clerk displayed the edict: long exile to Lanzhou — he immediately went to the place of banishment.

units.zh: 在嵐州逾年，清泰二年春，詔歸田里。
units.en: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of Qingtai 2 (935) an edict allowed him to return home.
units.literal: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of the second year of Qingtai an edict ordered him home to his native place.

units.zh: 妻紇幹氏塗中卒，讚比羸瘠，慟哭殆絕，因之亦病，行及石會關而卒，時年六十餘。
units.en: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the journey. Already frail, Zan wept until he nearly perished, fell ill himself, and died at Shihui Pass at over sixty years of age.
units.literal: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the road; Zan was already emaciated, wailed until nearly dead, and thereby also fell ill; traveling as far as Shihui Pass he died, aged over sixty.

units.zh: 史臣曰：自唐祚橫流，衣冠掃地，苟無端士，孰恢素風。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Once the Tang mandate ran awry and the scholar-official class was laid waste, only upright men could restore the old standards.
units.literal: The historiographer states: Since the Tang mandate flowed awry and the gentry were swept to the ground, if there were no upright scholars, who could restore the pure wind?

units.zh: 如廷珪之文學，崔沂之剛正，劉嶽之典禮，舜卿之掌誥，洎夢徵而下，皆蔚有貞規，無虧懿範，固可以為搢紳之圭表，聳朝廷之羽儀，以之垂名，夫何不韙。
units.en: Men such as Tinggui in letters, Yi in integrity, Yue in ritual, Shunqing in edict drafting, and from Mengzheng downward all upheld steadfast standards without blemish on their reputations. They may serve as models for the official class and ornaments of the court. To leave such names to posterity — what could be more fitting?
units.literal: Such as Tinggui's literary learning, Yi's stern uprightness, Yue's ritual regulations, Shunqing's control of edicts — down to Mengzheng and below — all richly possessed upright norms and did not fall short of fine models; they can indeed serve as standards for the gentry and as feathered banners for the court; to leave their names to posterity — how could that be wrong?

units.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
units.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
units.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

units.zh: 乙亥，翰林學士、工部侍郎竇夢徵卒。
units.en: On yihai Hanlin scholar and works vice minister Dou Mengzheng died.
units.literal: On yihai, Hanlin academician and Works Vice Minister Dou Mengzheng died.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 壬申，以成德軍節度行軍司馬、權知府事任圜為檢校右僕射、權北面水陸轉運製置使。
units.en: On renshen Ren Yuan, Chengde campaign marshal and acting prefect, became acting Right Vice Director and northern transport commissioner.
units.literal: On renshen, Chengde army campaign army marshal and acting prefect Ren Yuan was made acting Right Vice Director and acting northern land-and-water transport commissioner.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 乃以皇子繼岌為亞獻，皇弟存紀為終獻。
units.en: Jiji was made second libationer and Cunji final libationer.
units.literal: Prince Jiji was then made second libationer and the Emperor's brother Cunji final libationer.

units.zh: 幸左龍武軍，以皇子繼岌代張全義判六軍諸衛事故也。
units.en: Cunxu visited the Left Dragon Martial Army as Prince Jiji took over Zhang Quanyi's charge of the Six Armies and Guards.
units.literal: The Emperor visited the Left Dragon Martial Army because the prince Jiji was replacing Zhang Quanyi in overseeing the Six Armies and Imperial Guards.

units.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
units.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
units.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 進封河南尹兼河陽節度使張全義為魏王，兩浙節度使錢鏐進封吳越王。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi of Henan and Heyang was raised to Prince of Wei; Qian Liu of the two Zhes to King of Wu and Yue.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.

units.zh: 河南尹張全義進開平元年已前羨余錢十萬貫、綢六千匹、綿三十萬兩，仍請每年上供定額每歲貢絹三萬匹，以為常式。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi of Henan offered a hundred thousand strings of surplus coin from before Kaiping 1, six thousand bolts of silk, and three hundred thousand taels of cotton, and asked that thirty thousand bolts of silk yearly be fixed as tribute.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect, presented surplus money of one hundred thousand strings from before Kaiping year 1, six thousand bolts of silk, and three hundred thousand taels of cotton, and further requested a fixed annual tribute of thirty thousand bolts of silk as a standing rule.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 以太子詹事劉嶽為兵部侍郎，以太子右庶子王權為戶部侍郎，以太子左庶子任讚為工部侍郎。
units.en: Liu Yue, crown prince mentor, became War vice minister; Wang Quan, right vice mentor, Revenue vice minister; Ren Zan, left vice mentor, Works vice minister.
units.literal: Crown Prince Mentor Liu Yue was made Vice Minister of War; Crown Prince Right Vice Mentor Wang Quan was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Crown Prince Left Vice Mentor Ren Zan was made Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 乙丑，以刑部員外郎封翹為翰林學士。
units.en: On yichou, Feng Qiao of the Ministry of Punishments outer section entered the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: On yichou, Ministry of Punishments outer-section official Feng Qiao was made Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 秋七月丁巳，以淄州刺史陳洪為棣州刺史。
units.en: On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn, Chen Hong, prefect of Zi, was transferred to Di.
units.literal: On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn, Zi prefect Chen Hong was made Di prefect.

units.zh: 戊寅，至貝州，命四丞相及學士李琪、盧文度、知制誥竇賞等十五人扈從，其左常侍韋戩等二十三人止焉。
units.en: On wuyin he reached Beizhou and ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend; Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained behind.
units.literal: On wuyin he reached Beizhou, ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend, while Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained.

units.zh: 庚子，皇第二子金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒從榮可檢校太保、同平章事、天雄軍節度使、鄴都留守。
units.en: On gengzi the second prince Li Congrong—Gold and Purple Glory grand master and acting Minister of Education—could become acting Grand Guardian, co-equal councilor, Tianxiong commissioner, and Yedu regent.
units.literal: On gengzi, the Emperor's second son, Gold and Purple Glory Grand Master, acting Minister of Education Li Congrong could be made acting Grand Guardian, co-equal Chief Councilor, Tianxiong military commissioner, and Yedu regent.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：尚書兵部宣露布於樓前，宣訖，尚書刑部侍郎張文寶奏曰：「逆賊王都首級請付所司。」
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says War at the Secretariat proclaimed the bulletin at the tower; when it ended Zhang Wenbao of Punishments asked that Wang Du's head be given to the proper office."
units.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: The Ministry of War of the Secretariat proclaimed the victory bulletin before the tower; when the proclamation ended, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Zhang Wenbao memorialized: "The rebel Wang Du's head is requested to be delivered to the relevant office."
